name: Froglet public agent task manifest
purpose: Give HTTP-capable agents exact Froglet task contracts, evidence boundaries, and report fields before they run or recommend a hosted or local Froglet workflow.

task_contracts.title: Publish a selected catalog or Wasm function
task_contracts.when_to_use: The user wants their data or a small function usable by another agent.
steps: Prefer the existing native froglet MCP tool. Otherwise read only the Froglet agent configuration entry and use its exact binary and environment. Check --help and status; never assume PATH points to the configured installation. If setup is missing, use the exact immutable-release installation plan and separate approval.
Call native status from the actual agent; shell probes are not agent attachment.

Inspect source with prepare_service. Normalize mixed JSON to a separate named-row-collections file when necessary; preserve the original and report both paths. Propose relevant fields, clarify CSV types, and request an explicit destination.

Prepare a selected snapshot. Use only the advertised describe/select and scalar equals query contract; verify the example through Froglet itself. Show included/omitted fields, source fingerprint, example and actual local result.
Call marketplace_publish to obtain exact consent, then wait for publication approval.
Publish with that consent hash. Report local verification, public reachability, marketplace activation, and requester execution separately.
Return share_url with observed availability. Explain sleep/offline behavior and check_updates/open_status.
must_not_claim: public success while pending review
shell probe proves actual agent attachment
excluded data is absent without inspecting the snapshot
clean-machine or human qualification before it is run
automatic republication
managed always-on hosting
custom query simulation proves Froglet execution
a port conflict during preparation requires killing the healthy daemon
a prose consent invented by the agent authorizes publication

task_contracts.title: Use a shared service
task_contracts.when_to_use: The user provides a Froglet provider/service share link.
steps: Use the same native installation and separate installation approval if missing.
Resolve exact provider/service, validate HTTPS endpoint and signed offer, and obtain current public example input.
Call invoke_service with provider_id and service_id. Refuse paid offers.
Reconcile uncertain calls using the same idempotency_key and exact input.
Report result, receipt verification, and remaining uncertainty.
must_not_claim: webpage reachability proves recipient execution
marketplace data is live when stale
payment success on the free first-use path

task_contracts.title: Run or recover one bounded Wasm job
task_contracts.when_to_use: The user asks to run a supplied compatible Wasm program on a configured provider or inspect its existing task.
steps: Read the interoperability guide. Check tools/list on the exact configured native binary for run_compute and get_task; do not substitute an arbitrary binary from PATH.
Use only the user-selected program, JSON input and provider. Confirm compatible Wasm v1 and explicit execution authority. Default max_price_sats to 0; a paid ceiling alone is not spending authority.

Call native run_compute with exactly one of wasm_module_hex or wasm_module_path (an absolute local regular nonsymlink compiled file), explicit input, an exact nonblank idempotency_key and the selected provider. Preserve the key, program bytes, input and provider for reconciliation; changed work requires a new key.
If a Deal reference is returned, use get_task with task_id equal to that returned deal_id to inspect existing work without resubmitting or authorizing new payment.
Report submission intent separately from admitted work. An unresolved submission_pending intent is not success and must not be automatically replaced with a new-key submission.
Report the actual result and receipt_verification, noting that signed evidence does not independently establish result correctness or usefulness.
must_not_claim: every installed release contains the current source actions
an arbitrary A2A agent understands the required Froglet extension
localhost free tests qualify public or real-money deployment
a stdio test proves an actual IDE or LLM host is connected
a submission_pending reference proves provider admission
exact retries guarantee universally exactly-once execution
receipt verification proves computation truth or usefulness

task_contracts.title: Local artifact and chain verification
task_contracts.when_to_use: Use when the user provides signed Froglet artifacts and wants local cryptographic verification.
steps: Paste an artifact, array, or artifacts envelope
Run Verify evidence
Report every canonical artifact_type and its verification status
Report chain_evaluated, valid, and any structure_errors
must_not_claim: real-world provider identity
truthful execution or correct output
external payment settlement
current expiry unless explicitly checked
task_contracts.next_step: Checks signatures, canonical hashes, artifact semantics, and supplied chain links locally using WASM. Does not prove external settlement, real-world identity, truthful execution, or current expiry.

task_contracts.title: Marketplace evidence snapshot
task_contracts.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what the public marketplace currently shows or wants copyable evidence from the marketplace page.
required_capabilities: fetch marketplace JSON links when needed
copy or quote observed counts with timestamps
steps: Read the rendered marketplace counts
Record snapshot time, providers, offers, receipts, success rate, and indexed receipt value
Use the page copy action or JSON endpoints for source evidence
Avoid claiming hosted paid rails from marketplace counts alone
must_not_claim: hosted paid rails are live
mainnet money movement
production marketplace depth beyond observed public data
task_contracts.next_step: Use local install planning if the user wants to publish a service, consume private services, or test paid rails.

task_contracts.title: Local install proposal
task_contracts.when_to_use: Use when the user wants persistent identity, service publication, paid rails, private data workflows, batch, GPU, or Tor.
required_capabilities: use local MCP/OpenClaw planning tools when available
avoid running install commands before confirmation
allowed_hosts: local machine only after explicit user confirmation
steps: Report any evidence already observed, without claiming more
Ask for target agent, footprint, role, payment rail, network mode, marketplace, and first use case
Use plan_install before get_install_guide when local MCP tools exist
Verify local health before implementing the use case
must_not_claim: local installation was performed before commands actually ran
payment rails are live before adapter verification
GPU or batch production readiness before route-specific checks
task_contracts.next_step: After the profile is confirmed, produce exact commands and validation checks for the selected local path.

task_contracts.title: Chat-only fallback
task_contracts.when_to_use: Use when the model cannot fetch URLs, POST JSON, send Bearer auth, poll HTTP routes, run shell commands, or use MCP tools.
steps: Do not pretend to run Froglet
Tell the user to try the public beta in a browser or use an HTTP-capable agent with a local setup
Offer to interpret pasted outputs
must_not_claim: live Froglet evidence
a successful public beta run
verified receipt
task_contracts.next_step: Direct the user to the public beta in a browser or to an HTTP-capable agent with a local setup.
